scope: Source-supported management and window.odin contracts, not live readiness. Explicit METHODS plus Core CAPABILITIES, and every preload name including generated bridge tables.

rules.dispatch: Owners are fully-qualified classes or app symbols. status.get and turn_state.list use effective Core dispatch ahead of their composed management owners. Provider writes register via SettingsService and delegate to ProviderOwner. READ_METHODS, not method verbs, defines management read classification.
rules.capabilities: Gate actions on currently published core capabilities and owner readiness. computer-management-started means its private management state started and not closed. Native foreground input additionally requires explicit consent and reported X11 availability; cleanup publication is not native Wayland qualification.
rules.transactions: Retain owner revisions, confirmations, durable IDs, late receipts and unknown-effect protections. Never silently replay a write after stale revision, disconnect or unknown outcome.
rules.credentials: Leaf credentials use explicit write-only secrets.set/secrets.clear. secrets.unlock is explicit Retry only. Codex login/account actions own keyring transactions and preload exposes opaque login handles, not provider authorization secrets. Host transactions retain trust boundaries. Outbound webhook save/delete own signing-key/private-URL storage. Email get is a redacted observation, not a credential API.
rules.mcp_credentials: mcp.save owns headers_set/headers_remove, env_set/env_remove and private URL storage. Omitted fields retain credentials. mcp.delete clears owned containers. mcp.reconnect explicitly imports unlocked legacy credential presence; unmarked legacy credential edits require reconnect first. Generic settings.set and secrets.set are not MCP container APIs. Keep/replace/remove are UI intentions, not invented methods. No credential readback or blur-save.
rules.bridge_classification: MANAGEMENT declares skills.validate command=false while management READ_METHODS excludes it. Preserve this observed distinction. App read flags mean observation without user mutation/external action, not absence of caches or provider refresh activity.
rules.not_implemented: No invented runtime.restart or universal clear/export API. General Copy diagnostics composes only whitelisted desktop versions and current connection/engine facts through the existing copyText bridge; there is no new Core diagnostics API. Current app-local bridge actions getDesktopInfo, openSettingsFolder, exitOdin, getSetupReminderHidden and setSetupReminderHidden are app-owned, not Core methods: desktop info is a fixed public whitelist, folder open targets only the current profile config directory, exit reports acceptance of the existing bounded shutdown only, and setup dismissal reads/writes a profile-scoped app preference. Exit also exists through native menu/tray/launcher. runtime.reload scopes skills/config/context are not process restart. Slices 5 and 6 implement durable setup dismissal and window state; no planned preferences remain in this inventory.
rules.persistence: App state paths are profile-scoped; current entry selects the default profile with a global single-instance lock. Autostart is an OS desktop entry, not app-state.json. Drafts are app-owned content. Cleanup and identity journals are safety evidence, not user preferences.
